known.title: Decision Gap 7 posts the self-review as a `Code review` comment with a `Code-review:` verdict line, so the helper reads it as the latest trusted code-review verdict
known.locator: Research, Decisions, Gap 7 decision (line 30); Steps, row 7 yolo_rules (line 43)
known.summary: The Gap 7 decision makes the self-review return the code-review block shape (`### Code review round 0`, then a `Code-review:` verdict line, then its findings) and posts it unchanged as one issue comment before round 1. At repo_ref, the helper reads a comment as a review record when its first line names `code review` with any suffix and a later line holds `code-review: <verdict>` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs, REVIEW_HEADING and REVIEW_VERDICT at lines 613-614, parseReviewComment at lines 619-643; plan-contract.md lines 155-178, which allow any suffix such as `round 2`). reviewVerdicts (plan.mjs lines 644-656) keeps the latest comment per kind whose author is the only assignee, and the yolo manager is that assignee and posts every comment. So `show <n>` prints `code=pass` from the manager's own self-review before any code-reviewer round. A local run of parseReviewComment from repo_ref on `### Code review round 0` and `Code-review: pass` gave kind code, verdict pass; it gave pass also with a finding line `HIGH · Bug · <file>:<line>` in the docks code-review report format (plugins/docks/skills/engineering/code-review/SKILL.md lines 108-113), because severeFinding (plan.mjs lines 615-618) reads only `[high]`, `high:`, or `severity: high`. The yolo Run order ends Code review when `show <n>` reads `code=pass` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md line 67), and a run that recovers after compaction takes the verdicts from `show` and counts review rounds from issue comments (lines 217-224). No step changes the helper's review-record reader, and step 7 edits only yolo/SKILL.md. So the self-review can stand in for the independent code review, and the round count includes a round 0.

known.title: Decision Gap 10 adds a third merge option, `Merge and continue`, to yolo, but no step changes the contract's two-option merge question
known.locator: Research, Decisions, Gap 10 decision (line 28); Steps, row 5 contract_rules, Task (line 41); Steps, row 7 yolo_rules, Files (line 43)
known.summary: The Gap 10 decision gives the yolo merge question a third option, `Merge and continue`, and merges on it. Step 7 edits only plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md, and step 5 states only the gap 2, 3, 11, 12, and 13 rules and the yolo adopt pointer in the contract. At repo_ref, the canonical contract also owns the merge question: plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md lines 308-312 say 'Ask afresh with two options: `Merge now` and `Leave pull request open`. Without `Merge now`, leave the issue and the pull request open', and its Yolo runs Merge question (lines 407-411) tells a yolo run to ask the question in Checks and merge. plan-manager/SKILL.md lines 142-144 ('ask afresh for `Merge now` or `Leave pull request open`, and merge only on `Merge now`') and the root AGENTS.md line 81 ('Merge needs a fresh `Merge now` answer') state the same rule. plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md lines 63-68 make the contract canonical and ask for coordinated edits across these surfaces when a concept changes. After the plan, yolo merges on `Merge and continue`, while the contract that yolo loads (yolo/SKILL.md lines 21-23) tells the same run to leave the pull request open on every answer other than `Merge now`. The plan must also change the contract, plan-manager/SKILL.md, and AGENTS.md, or keep the two options.

known.title: Acceptance A2 runs only the plan-lifecycle plugin gate, but steps 1-4 change scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs, for which the root AGENTS.md requires the full gate
known.locator: Acceptance, A2 (line 54); Steps, rows 1-4 research_gate, edit_retry, shared_files, rereview_advice, Files and Done when (lines 37-40)
known.summary: A2 runs `node scripts/ci.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle` per commit and on the reviewed head, and no Done when cell or Acceptance row runs the full gate. Steps 1-4 change scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs, which is outside every plugin root. At repo_ref, the root AGENTS.md (Tool-agnostic rules, lines 98-99) keeps the plugin gate for a change owned by exactly one plugin and requires full `node scripts/ci.mjs` for repo-wide validation or tooling, shared infrastructure used by multiple plugins, and changes that span plugins. scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs is such a file: both the docks and the plan-lifecycle descriptors select it through the `plan-reviewer` author check (scripts/lib/plugins.mjs lines 66 and 88-90), the docks descriptor owns the Biome scope `scripts` (lines 56-58), and the CI resolver treats a change under scripts/ as a change to every shard (scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs lines 125-128). With `--plugin plan-lifecycle`, ci.mjs runs `biome ci` only on plugins/plan-lifecycle/test and `biome lint` only on the plan-manager scripts (scripts/ci.mjs lines 233-251; scripts/lib/plugins.mjs lines 78-81), and it skips the repo-wide sections. Only the full gate runs `bun run check:js`, which runs `biome ci scripts ...` (package.json line 12). So no gate of the plan checks the format and the repo-wide rules of the changed scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs before the pull request.

known.title: Decision Gap 11 says that Research 'holds' the placeholder, which leaves substring or whole-section matching to the implementer, and the two choices give different `status` results
known.locator: Research, Decisions, Gap 11 decision (line 23); Steps, row 1 research_gate (line 37); Acceptance, A3 (line 55)
known.summary: The Gap 11 decision makes `status` refuse `planned` and `ongoing` while Research 'is empty or holds `_Not researched yet._`', and makes the drafting advice use the same test. It does not say if 'holds' means that the section is only the placeholder or that the placeholder occurs in it. At repo_ref, the drafting advice uses a substring test: printAdvice runs `parsePlan(text).sections.get('Research').includes('_Not researched yet._')` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs lines 598-602), so an implementer who reuses it builds a substring gate. A filled Research can quote the placeholder in prose: this plan's own Research does (line 23). A local run of parsePlan from repo_ref on this body gave `includes` true and trimmed equality false. With a substring test, `status <n> planned` and `status <n> ongoing` exit 1 for a researched plan such as this one, and the advice still prints for it; with a whole-section test they succeed. A3 (line 55) checks only a Research section that is the placeholder, which both choices refuse, so no Acceptance row fixes the observable result.
